historical_references.reference: Makbul was a Yadava king who ruled over the Delhi Sultanate during the late 13th century. He gained prominence after defeating the Mongol invader, Qutlugh Khwaja, and became a vassal of the Khilji dynasty.

historical_references.reference: Makbul is also mentioned in the 'Ain-i-Akbari', a Persian-language document of the Mughal Empire, as the founder of the Makbulpur village in the modern-day Haryana state of India. The village is believed to have been established in the late 16th century during the reign of Akbar.
